newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil demand to rise 0.5 pct/yr to 2005 - WoodMac.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil demand to rise 0.5 pct/yr to 2005 - WoodMac.

text.p: Oil demand in 19 OECD-member European countries is forecast to grow at an average rate of 0.5 to 0.6 percent per year to 2005, analysts Wood Mackenzie said on Thursday.

Demand, predicted at 0.6 percent annually in 1996-2000 and 0.5 percent in 2001-2005, will grow fastest in Turkey, Denmark and Greece, the consultancy said in its European Oil Downstream Review for 1996.
"Economic upturn is now being seen across many European countries, boosting demand particularly in the industrial and transportation sectors," the report said.
The forecasts compare to demand growth of 1.3 percent recorded in 1991-95 and 0.6 percent in 1987-1990, the report said.

Oil demand in Turkey and Greece continues to be driven by rapid economic development while Denmark has shown a marked increase due to a switch from coal to orimulsion in power generation, the report said.
The report predicts demand growth in Turkey of 3.8 percent in 1996-2000 and 1.9 percent in 2001-2005, followed by Denmark with 2.3 percent and zero respectively.
Greek demand will grow at 1.9 percent and 1.7 percent respectively, the consultancy said.
The main area of growth remains middle distillates, particularly in transport, due to rising use of diesel cars and jet kerosene in aviation.

Gasoline demand is expected to continue to increase very slowly to 2005, with strong growth of more than two percent a year in Portugal, Ireland, Turkey, Greece and Spain counter-balancing declines in most other countries after the turn of the century.
The report forecast gasoline demand growth at 0.4 percent in 1996-2000 and 0.2 percent in 2001-2005, with the strongest rates forecast in Portugal, followed by Ireland and Turkey.

"In general diesel cars are increasingly gaining acceptance as economical environmentally-friendly alternatives to gasoline vehicles and this trend has been behind the steady increase in demand for diesel in the transport sector," the report said.
The analysts forecast gasoline demand to read 130 million tonnes by 2000 compared to 127 million tonnes in 1995.

Within the overall total, large differences will emerge in the demand patterns between the well-developed Western economies where gasoline demand is stagnant, and emerging markets such as Greece, Portugal and Turkey.
In the emerging markets, gasoline is expected to rise by an average of four to five percent annually and in the developed economies of northwest Europe to fall by 0.5 percent annually in 1996-2000.
